At Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC) in 2021, Apple announced support for storing driver's licenses in Apple Wallet on iPhone. At the time, Apple marketed this feature as the final step to letting you "completely ditch your physical wallet."

Here are the upcoming states for Apple Wallet driver's license support……

Apple Wallet ID Support

Over the five years since Apple announced the feature, support has gradually expanded across the United States. Currently, iPhone and Apple Watch users in 14 states and Puerto Rico can add a driver's license or state ID to Apple Wallet. The full list is available here:

Where will this feature launch first? Here's what we know so far.

The following seven states have confirmed they are working on Apple Wallet driver's license support, and have been listed as partners by Apple and/or appeared in Apple's code:

  • Kentucky (launching in the "summer" of 2026)
  • North Carolina (launching in early 2027)
  • Oklahoma (in development, no launch date set)
  • Utah (in development, no launch date set)
  • Virginia (in development, no launch date set)
  • Connecticut (progress unknown, previously listed as a partner by Apple)
  • Mississippi (progress unknown, previously listed as a partner by Apple)

Meanwhile, the Secure Technology Alliance has been tracking the rollout of mobile driver's license support across the United States. The following states have begun exploring mobile ID support through legislation or research, but have not yet been mentioned by Apple:

  • Indiana
  • Vermont
  • New Jersey
  • Florida
  • South Carolina
  • Tennessee
  • Missouri
  • Nevada
  • Wyoming

It's worth noting that progress varies significantly from state to state. A state exploring or developing digital ID support does not necessarily mean it will ultimately launch, let alone make its way to Apple Wallet.

Summary

As you can see, Apple Wallet driver's license support is still rolling out fairly sporadically across the United States.

However, even if your state doesn't yet support Apple Wallet's digital ID feature, you don't have to wait in vain.

Apple launched a new "Digital ID" feature last year, powered by a U.S. passport. While it's not your driver's license, it does let you use your iPhone at TSA checkpoints at over 250 airports across the country.

Do you have an ID or driver's license stored in Apple Wallet on your iPhone? Have you actually used it? Let us know in the comments.
